lines.text:
Exploring the Space Center

During the school holidays, my father took me and my brother to the National Space Center. It was a three-hour drive, but the visit was worth every minute.

The first thing we saw was a full-size replica of a rocket standing outside the building. Inside, the ground floor had an exhibition about the history of space exploration. We learned that the first person in space was Yuri Gagarin in 1961, and the first moon landing was in 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission.

Upstairs, there was an interactive section where visitors could try on a spacesuit and sit in a mock-up of a spacecraft cockpit. The spacesuit was surprisingly heavy — astronauts train for months to get used to working in them.

The planetarium was my favourite part. We sat in reclining chairs while a dome-shaped screen above us showed a film about the solar system. We flew past Jupiter's moons, through Saturn's rings, and out to the edge of the Milky Way. It felt like we were really floating in space.

There was also a section about the International Space Station. A display showed what astronauts eat — dried food in pouches that they add water to. Another screen showed how astronauts exercise in zero gravity to keep their muscles strong.

Before we left, we visited the gift shop and I bought a poster of the planets. My brother got a freeze-dried ice cream packet — the same kind astronauts eat!

The visit inspired me to learn more about astronomy. Maybe one day I will work for a space agency.

lines.name: ✅ "The Earth orbits the Sun..." / "...revolves around the Sun."

lines.text: While 'goes around' is understood, the precise scientific terms are 'orbit' or 'revolve around'. 'Rotate' means spin on its own axis.

lines.text: ✅ "There is microgravity in space." / "Astronauts experience weightlessness."
lines.name: ✅ "There is microgravity in space." / "Astronauts experience weightlessness."

lines.text: Gravity exists everywhere in space — it's what keeps the Moon orbiting Earth. Astronauts float because they're in free fall, not because gravity is absent.

lines.text: 'Wear' is irregular: wear–wore–worn. There is no 'weared'.

lines.text: NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) is the US space agency. ESA (European Space Agency) represents 22 European countries. The UK Space Agency is a member of ESA. Russia's agency is Roscosmos.

lines.text: British: 'centre' / American: 'center'. British: 'programme' / American: 'program'. British: 'colour' / American: 'color'. In space science, American terminology dominates globally.

lines.text: 'Astronaut' is used in English-speaking countries. 'Cosmonaut' is the Russian term. 'Taikonaut' is sometimes used for Chinese astronauts. All three words refer to space travellers.
